title: Vintage Fender Jazz Bass Value Guide: 1960 To 1979 Prices
description: Vintage Fender Jazz Bass values by year from 1960 to 1979, with stack-knob and later era ranges, condition and repair notes, and photos from my archive.
h1: Vintage Fender Jazz Bass Value Guide
alt: Lake Placid Blue Fender Jazz Bass body with white pickguard and chrome covers

faqs.q: How Much Is A Vintage Fender Jazz Bass Worth?
faqs.a: As of October 2026, the comparisons span $2,000 to $29,000 across 1960 to 1979. Original sunburst stack-knob instruments use a $21,000 to $29,000 reference, while the late-1970s standard-finish comparison is $2,000 to $4,000. Each band has its own condition and case allowances.

faqs.q: What Is A 1966 Fender Jazz Bass Worth?
faqs.a: The shared 1965 to 1969 sunburst comparison is $4,500 to $12,000. It allows differing wear and minor hardware changes while retaining original finish, pickups and case. A specific 1966 bass needs its actual fingerboard configuration and condition assessed; the full era range isn't a separate bound-dot premium.

faqs.q: What Is A 1972 Fender Jazz Bass Worth?
faqs.a: The 1970 to 1974 sunburst range is $3,500 to $6,000, with original finish, pickups and case. A professional refret and replacement nut can fit within that category. I assess repairs and substantial modifications separately.

faqs.q: Why Do Some Years Share A Price Range?
faqs.a: Adjacent years can share an era range. I assess the exact configuration and condition before narrowing it. The condition notes explain which guitars each band covers.

faqs.q: Does A Quality Refret Change The Originality Category?
faqs.a: A quality refret is accepted maintenance and preserves the all-original classification of an otherwise all-original bass. It takes the instrument out of the museum-quality category. Neck reshaping and substantial fingerboard alterations are separate changes.

faqs.q: Does A Refinish Have A Fixed Percentage Deduction?
faqs.a: No. A refinish changes the collector comparison, but the year, retained parts, structural condition and quality of the work still need to be assessed. I don't use one percentage for every modified bass.

faqs.q: Is A Dealer Offer The Same As The Guide Range?
faqs.a: No. The guide is a market comparison with stated conditions. An offer has its own terms, included accessories and responsibilities. Private-sale proceeds also depend on fees, shipping and the final agreement.

faqs.q: Should I Replace Parts Before An Appraisal?
faqs.a: Start by documenting the bass as it is. Keep removed parts, photographs and repair records together. I don't need cosmetic restoration or unfamiliar disassembly before an initial appraisal.
